title: Administrative penalty system and accountability reports
subtitle: Integrity Commissioner and Lobbyist Registrar annual reports, internal audit plan, cemetery appointment, heritage plaques, provincial election reminder.
overview: Council approved the by-laws, policies and fees for a new Administrative Penalty System as part of the consent report. The system sets up screening and hearing officers and designates specified by-laws as subject to administrative penalties. Staff were directed to add the new fees to the User Fees By-law as soon as practical. Council also approved the Internal Audit Work Plan for 2025 to 2027.

Council received the first annual report of the Lobbyist Registrar and the fourth annual report of the Integrity Commissioner. The Integrity Commissioner reported four code of conduct complaints in 2024 and no applications under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act. Proposed code of conduct amendments are expected at the March 4 meeting.

After a closed session on public appointments, Council appointed David Kennedy to the Guelph Cemetery Commission for a term ending November 2026. Council also recognized owners of heritage-designated properties, who received plaques. The Mayor encouraged residents to vote in the provincial election on Thursday, February 27.

decisions.detail: Council approved the by-laws, policies and fees to establish an Administrative Penalty System, including screening and hearing officer positions, and directed staff to add the fees to the User Fees By-law {{vote:m5}}.
Council approved the Internal Audit Work Plan for 2025 to 2027 as part of the consent report {{vote:m6}}.
Council appointed David Kennedy to the Guelph Cemetery Commission for a term ending November 2026 or until a successor is appointed {{vote:m2}}.
Council received the 2024 Annual Report of the Integrity Commissioner {{vote:m7}}.
Council received the first annual report of the Lobbyist Registrar, covering 2024 {{vote:m8}}.

debate: The Integrity Commissioner said the complaints came from members of the public, not from councillors, in response to a councillor's question.

A councillor asked about a provision in Guelph's code of conduct that requires a formal report when advice reveals a possible contravention. The Integrity Commissioner called it unusual and not seen in other codes, but said it need not be removed right away.

On what counts as a significant interest, the Integrity Commissioner said a very small amount, such as a nominal membership fee, would likely be too minor to matter. They advised members to ask in writing when unsure, since the dollar value alone is not the test.
The Integrity Commissioner said further code of conduct revisions are on hold while staff wait to see whether the province revives a uniform code like the one proposed in Bill 241.

The Lobbyist Registrar said the registry aims to regulate access and add transparency, not restrict it. Procurement, planning processes and communications at the city's invitation are not treated as lobbying, and no formal complaints were received.
